display.purpose: App name on setup screen, completion headline. Big and settled.

label.purpose: Button text, interactive labels. Weight 500 for readability at action size.

caption.purpose: Comparison count, stage indicator, metadata. Intentionally quiet.

motion.name: tap-feedback
motion.purpose: Photo cell tap confirmation. Scale pulse tells the user the choice landed before the next pair arrives.

motion.name: pair-transition
motion.purpose: Next photo pair arriving. Fast enough to feel snappy, slow enough to register as a real new comparison.

motion.name: screen-transition
motion.purpose: Full app state changes: setup → comparing → complete → results.

motion.name: button-hover
motion.purpose: Primary button hover/press color shift. No scale, no shadow.

motion.name: ease-out-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all transitions. Exits fast, stops crisply.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary CTA per screen. Terracotta fill, Film White Fraunces label.
components.css: @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:wght@400;500;600&display=swap'); .ds-btn-primary { background: oklch(57% 0.125 62); color: oklch(97% 0.008 65); font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.01em; line-height: 1.3; padding: 14px 20px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 80ms cubic-bezier(0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(52% 0.125 62); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(57% 0.125 62); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: oklch(50% 0.125 62); transform: scale(0.98); }

components.name: Primary Button Disabled
components.description: Primary CTA in its unavailable state. Not interactive-looking.
components.css: @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:wght@400;500;600&display=swap'); .ds-btn-primary-disabled { background: oklch(85% 0.008 65); color: oklch(52% 0.008 65); font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.01em; line-height: 1.3; padding: 14px 20px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 1; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary actions: Skip to Results, Start Over, See Full Rankings. Quiet but present.
components.css: @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:wght@400;500;600&display=swap'); .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: oklch(52% 0.008 65); font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.3; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: color 80ms cubic-bezier(0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: oklch(35% 0.010 65); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(57% 0.125 62); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Photo Comparison Cell
components.description: The core UI element. Near-frameless photo presented as a print. Fills full width, 4:3 aspect ratio.
components.css: .ds-photo-cell { position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 4/3; border-radius: 4px; overflow: hidden; background: oklch(93% 0.010 65); cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 120ms cubic-bezier(0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0); } .ds-photo-cell:active { opacity: 0.88; transform: scale(0.97); transition: transform 60ms cubic-bezier(0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0), opacity 60ms; } .ds-photo-cell-img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; } .ds-photo-overlay-btn { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; background: oklch(10% 0 0 / 55%); border: none; border-radius: 100px; padding: 8px; cursor: pointer; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; transition: background 80ms; } .ds-photo-overlay-btn:hover { background: oklch(10% 0 0 / 75%); }

components.description: Session complete indicator in comparison toolbar.
components.css: @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:wght@400;500;600&display=swap'); .ds-badge-complete { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: oklch(55% 0.12 145 / 15%); color: oklch(35% 0.09 145); font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.02em; line-height: 1.3; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 100px; }

components.description: Thin strip above comparison cells while upload is in progress. Quiet by design.
components.css: @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:wght@400;500;600&display=swap'); .ds-upload-banner { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 8px 16px; background: oklch(93% 0.010 65); } .ds-upload-track { flex: 1; height: 2px; background: oklch(85% 0.008 65); border-radius: 100px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-upload-fill { height: 100%; background: oklch(57% 0.125 62); border-radius: 100px; transition: width 300ms ease-out; } .ds-upload-label { font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 400; color: oklch(52% 0.008 65); letter-spacing: 0.02em; white-space: nowrap; }

narrative.overview:
Pictalis is the quiet room where a batch of 200 photos gets edited down to the twelve you'll actually keep. The interface should feel like sitting under a single lamp with a stack of prints and a marker — warm, private, unhurried in spirit but quick in motion. Everything that isn't a photo exists to move you toward the next choice. Decoration is forbidden; the grain is in the palette.

The type is Fraunces throughout — a variable-weight optical serif with organic warmth that resists the cold precision of the default iOS sans-serif. At display sizes it feels editorial, like a photo zine. At label sizes it has just enough character to remind you this isn't a file manager. Motion is fast but not mechanical: pairs arrive at 120ms ease-out, giving a sense of momentum rather than instant teleportation. A session should feel like forward motion, not checklist processing.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white base — aged paper, not clinical white
Single accent color (amber) used sparingly; photos supply all other color
Fraunces at every text size — weight contrast replaces typeface switching
Photos presented as near-frameless prints (4px radius, maximum surface area)
Motion snappy at 120ms, never mechanical; screen transitions at 220ms

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Terracotta appears on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. Never use it for decoration — only for the single most important action in the current context.

rules.name: The No-White Rule
rules.body: Never use pure #ffffff or #000000. Film White and Ink have been calibrated with warm undertones; straying to pure values breaks the photographic feel.

rules.name: The Weight-Over-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is expressed through weight contrast first, size second. Two type sizes with two weight levels are enough for the entire UI. Resist adding a third typeface.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If you're reaching for a shadow, ask whether tonal layering (a background step from Film White to Grain Paper, or Grain Paper to Divider) solves the problem instead. Usually it does.

dos: Do present photos at maximum possible size. The frame should feel like looking through a window, not a thumbnail preview.
Do use Terracotta for exactly one interactive element per screen — the primary action. Its singularity is what makes it work.
Do use weight contrast (400 → 600) to create hierarchy within Fraunces before reaching for size differences.
Do keep motion snappy: 120ms ease-out for pair transitions, 60ms for tap feedback, 220ms for full-screen transitions.
Do use Film White and Grain Paper — not pure #fff or #f5f5f5 — to maintain the warm-paper feel throughout.
Do write copy that honors that these are personal memories. 'Your favorites are ready' not 'Processing complete.'
donts: Don't use gradient fills on any background, button, or text element. This is explicitly the Generic SaaS anti-reference from PRODUCT.md.
Don't apply background-clip: text with a gradient for any heading — not the app name, not the completion headline, nowhere.
Don't make the comparison UI feel like Tinder. No swipe gestures, no gamified streak counters, no points or badges.
Don't let the chrome compete with the photos. If a UI element is drawing your eye away from the images, it's too loud.
Don't use #ffffff or #000000. Every color in this system has a warm undertone; pure white or pure black will read as foreign.
Don't use a shadow on any surface. Elevation is tonal or photographic, never shadow-based.
Don't introduce a border-left stripe as an accent on any list item, card, or callout.
Don't add status indicators or comparison counts that quantify the process in ways that feel mechanical.
